durable_exchange: Added one additive auth_credential_refresh_exchanges table: credential_id primary key, generation, owner, expected_hash, replacement_data. Generation and expected row bytes are SHA-256 fingerprints; no additional plaintext R0 copy is persisted.

Reservation is created only after an actual future refresh passes freshness/canRefresh/cancellation checks and obtains ownership, immediately before invoking the refresh callback. Reservation failure prevents invocation.

A same-generation pending reservation is never renewed into permission to redeem again. Lease expiry, process restart, response loss, timeout and HTTP 503 do not authorize another application-level send for that generation.

A known successful result is staged before credential publication. Publication and reservation retirement are one transaction, fenced by the current lease, unchanged original row, and exact staged replacement.

Only the immutable exchange owner can stage its result. Staging can finish after its write lease expires but cannot update the credential row. A subsequent lease owner may publish that already-staged result without another token request.

The durable owner bounds its wait without racing away the provider result before the staging continuation. Late successful responses are still staged. A failed staging write retains the result in memory for persistence retry, not another exchange.

redemption_and_storage_trace: Key selection eager preflight and final-candidate resolution -> OAuthRefresher.refresh -> per-id singleflight -> owned stored refresh -> durable reservation -> local/custom registry dispatch -> stage -> renewed, fenced commit. Selection only resynchronizes the winning row afterwards.
OAuthAccounts.refresh -> refreshById -> the same singleflight/owner path. Its return is read-only and redacted; it does not remerge a caller snapshot into storage.
Usage near-expiry preflight and health's expired-token preflight -> the same refresher. UsageService.persistRefreshedCredential refuses lease-backed secondary writes; health uses that helper.

Broker scheduler and POST /v1/credential/:id/refresh -> OAuthAccounts.refresh. Remote-store/client delegation carries reason; the CLI's overrideMints:true local override executes registry refresh or managed MCP refresh under the broker's durable owner.

Managed MCP local path -> oauth.refreshStored with subtype-aware canRefresh/merge -> refreshManagedMcpOAuthCredential -> refreshMCPOAuthToken. Its broker path delegates by id into the same durable owner. The MCP helper performs one token fetch, not a token retry loop.

Built-in registry request refresh -> postTokenRequest, which makes one application-level token POST. Cursor's hook makes one refresh POST; Snowflake makes one refresh POST; Copilot's helper preserves its non-rotating credential behavior. Registered custom callbacks must honor the documented one-attempt contract.

Public low-level registry/MCP token helpers remain provider primitives, not storage owners. The internal storage callers found converge through the owner above; callers deliberately invoking those primitives outside AuthStorage are outside the journal guarantee. Broker HTTP retry can request a later, successfully persisted generation, but an unresolved generation cannot be re-exchanged through the guarded owner.
reports.safety_argument: [INFERENCE, source-backed; not executed] For a stored generation G, the atomic reservation is durable before the callback that can send G. A later owner seeing that reservation either publishes its exact known staged replacement or fails without invoking the callback. Reservation is not cleared on timeout, response loss or lease release; therefore those events do not cause an additional application-level redemption of G. Full-row and generation fences prevent an old result from poisoning or overwriting a concurrent login/logout/replacement. This is not provider exactly-once semantics and does not establish server consumption, revocation, transport-level retransmission or idempotency behavior.

availability_and_deployment.tradeoff: An admitted callback is conservatively ambiguous after failure, including 503 or a crash between reservation and actual send. Automatic refresh of that generation is unavailable until a known replacement can be recovered or the user reauthenticates. Already-aborted callers, lease-wait cancellation, freshness short-circuits and canRefresh refusal create no reservation. Failure after invocation is not inferred to be pre-send merely from its error name.
availability_and_deployment.known_result_limit: A committed staged replacement survives credential-publication failure and is recoverable without resending R0. If storage itself cannot stage a known result, it is retained in memory while that process survives; a crash before any successful staging commit can still require reauthentication. The durable reservation continues to prevent blind reuse.
availability_and_deployment.mixed_runtime_limit: The additive table is schema-compatible with older readers, but old auth writers do not implement its protocol and can redeem an ambiguous generation. Drain/stop every old auth writer, including broker/gateway processes, before enabling the new runtime. A rollback to an unprotected writer is not a credential-safe recovery mechanism. Preserve the current credential DB and never restore older token bytes.
availability_and_deployment.production_boundary: No production database, credentials, login, refresh, usage or external provider request was accessed or exercised.

implementation.durable_refresh: Future admitted local refreshes reserve a generation fingerprint durably before invoking redemption. Pending generations cannot be redeemed again after ambiguous failure, lease takeover, or restart. Known replacements are staged with original-owner and current-row fencing, then published only by the current lease owner through an atomic staged-result commit.
implementation.cancellation: Waiter cancellation does not cancel the admitted owner or discard late successful results. Already-aborted calls, cancelled lease waits, fresh credentials, and canRefresh refusals do not reserve a generation.

safety_scope.claim: Static implementation argument: an unresolved reserved generation cannot invoke another redemption through the durable auth owner. This is not a claim of provider exactly-once semantics.
safety_scope.availability_tradeoff: Failures after invocation, including HTTP 503, remain ambiguous and prevent automatic redemption of that generation. A staged replacement permits recovery without another POST; otherwise sign-in or proven recovery is required. A crash after reservation but before transmission conservatively sacrifices availability.
safety_scope.mixed_runtime_limitation: Schema changes are additive, but old auth writers do not honor the journal. Deployment must drain all old writers, including broker/gateway processes, without modifying token data.

Broker refresh returns the complete current redacted row, including intentional field absence. Refresh, selection, usage, and health recognize both local lease ownership and authoritative upstream ownership, adopting the winning row rather than merging stale metadata or writing it again.

An admitted delegated refresh has its own bounded 10-second owner lifetime. Individual signals only cancel their respective waits; the initiating waiter cannot cancel the shared broker fetch. An unchanged refresh secret is encoded as refresh:null in replacement_data, referring to the exact hash-fenced active row rather than copying R0. Recovery reconstructs the secret only after row/hash matching; staging comparison and commit use the same encoding.
